config.description: Your personal overview: hours, leave, expenses and payslips.
config._note: hrmq-personal-dashboard (design.md D1/D3): the caller-scoped personal landing surface hydra ADR-097 Decision 3 requires — 'route to a type: "dashboard" page scoped to the caller … Not an index page, and not a bare parent with no route of its own'. The MijnHrGroup menu entry gains route: "MijnHr" through this fragment's menu block (mergeMenuItems fills the base group's undefined route key), so the group title lands here while its nine children stay under the collapse chevron — both of Decision 3's conditions, which moves humaniq's counted main-menu total from 6 to 5. Every widget carries a caller-scope filter (userId: "@me", or managerUserId: "@me" for the approver's own queue) plus the OPTIONAL administration token @workspace.activeAdministrationId? — unresolved means dropped, so a widget degrades to user-scoped-only, never to another user's rows. Only the built-in `stat` and `object-table` types are used (stat resolves through humaniq's own registry.js override, which is load-bearing: the library's self-registration is tree-shaken out of the production bundle); no custom widget, no new backend endpoint, no raw-GraphQL dataSource (the steering Dashboard's _note documents why that form resolves a schema by name across every register on the instance). Widget 6 has no conditional-visibility primitive available — the dashboard widget grammar has none for stat tiles (design.md D4) — so it always renders and shows 0 for a caller who manages nobody; its caption keeps the zero legible. The stat tiles' click-through uses content.route in the vue-router LOCATION-OBJECT form ({"name": "…"}), not the bare string design.md D3 writes: widgetLink passes a string straight to <router-link :to>, where vue-router 4 reads it as a PATH, so a bare route NAME would fall through to the catch-all. Same spelling the hr-objects nav-card entries already use. The three object-table widgets carry the FLAT content contract (register/schema/filter/sort{field,dir}/limit/columns/rowRoute/viewAllRoute/emptyText), NOT the nested `source` shape design.md D3 writes — measured live 2026-08-22, not inferred: on a type:"dashboard" page CnDashboardPage.registryRenderer looks up getWidgetTypeEntry(canonicalWidgetType(type)), and utils/widgetTypeAliases.js maps `object-table` -> `table`, which registerDashboardWidgets.js registers INLINE to CnObjectListWidget. The alias therefore never reaches CnWidgetObjectTable's dashboardRegistration (its `object-table` key is registered under a name the canonicaliser has already rewritten away, in a side-effect module ADR-061 tree-shaking drops anyway). With the `source` shape the widget rendered its emptyText and fired ZERO fetches, because CnObjectListWidget reads content.register/content.schema and has no `source` key at all. Consequences of the real contract, accepted: `limit` is a FETCH CAP (ADR-062), not a render promise — the visible row count fits the cell — and there is no per-row-route escape, which is fine since rowRoute is already a single static route name. All three also carry allowCreate: false — CnObjectListWidget renders a "+ Toevoegen" create affordance by DEFAULT (measured live), and all three collections are read-only to the employee: Timesheets are server-created by the booking flow (MijnUrenstaten already sets showAdd: false), LeaveBalance is written only by LeaveAccrualJob, and payslips are payroll-generated (REQ-MHS-004's read-only posture). Labels are Dutch literals; hrmq-i18n-locale-completeness owns their conversion and this change adds no English keys.
